title: U.S. House · Colorado's 5th District
area: El Paso County, including Colorado Springs and the Pikes Peak region.

context.text: Incumbent Jeff Crank (R) won the June 30, 2026 Republican primary unopposed after several announced candidates, including former U.S. Rep. Doug Lamborn, withdrew or did not qualify for the ballot. Jessica Killin defeated Joe Reagan in the Democratic primary. Ballotpedia's race ratings as of late September 2026 range from "Tilt Republican" to "Likely Republican."

candidates.name: Jeff Crank

summary.text: Jeff Crank is the Republican incumbent for Colorado's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2024 to succeed Doug Lamborn. A Colorado native, he was a congressional staffer, Colorado Springs Chamber of Commerce executive, Americans for Prosperity executive and radio host before entering Congress. He sits on the Armed Services and Natural Resources committees.

background.text: Born in Pueblo, Colorado, in 1967, according to Ballotpedia; his official biography says he was born and raised in southern Colorado, the son of a school teacher's aide and a World War II Navy veteran who later managed a missile program at the Pueblo Army Depot.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Colorado State University in 1990.

Worked in Washington, D.C., for Rep. Joel Hefley from 1991 to 1998, focusing on military issues and serving as administrative director; his official biography says he helped author the Military Family Housing Privatization Act.
Returned to Colorado to serve as vice president, later senior vice president, of the Colorado Springs Chamber of Commerce.
Later worked as chief operating officer at Americans for Prosperity (Ballotpedia describes the role as Colorado state director) and as president of his own real estate investment company.
Has a broadcasting background, hosting The Jeff Crank Show on a Colorado Springs radio station and the American Potential Podcast.
Won the June 25, 2024 Republican primary over Dave Williams, 65.2% to 34.8%, and the November 2024 general election with 54.7% to 40.9% for the Democratic nominee, succeeding Doug Lamborn.
Committee assignments for 2025-2026 are Armed Services and Natural Resources.
Advanced from the June 30, 2026 Republican primary unopposed; his official biography says he and his wife, Lisa, have two children.

priorities.text: In an interview, said he sees the race as a choice between a candidate focused on opposing President Trump and one focused on representing the community regardless of who is president.
priorities.quote: The question, and I think this will be one in this race, is, does this community just want somebody who's anti-Trump to fight and push back on Trump? Or do they want somebody who, no matter who the president is, whether it's Joe Biden or Donald Trump, is going to go try and work to represent this community and get the best things for this community that they can?

priorities.text: Lowering health care premium costs, citing his vote for the Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act, which he says offers alternatives to extending ACA subsidies.
Keeping electricity and energy costs low by advancing grid reliability measures, citing his vote for the Grid Power Act.

positions.summary: Voted against extending enhanced Affordable Care Act premium subsidies without what he called serious reform, saying Congress should focus on lowering costs and expanding competition instead.
positions.quote: I cannot support an extension of the ACA subsidies without serious reform. Congress cannot keep writing a blank check to Obamacare and slapping a subsidy band-aid on a healthcare system that remains fundamentally unaffordable. Congress needs to focus on real reforms that lower costs, improve and expand competition so consumers have real choices.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources (Energy and Mineral Resources; Water, Wildlife and Fisheries subcommittees) and the House Committee on Armed Services (Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation; Military Personnel; Strategic Forces subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.

candidates.researchNotes: Issue positions above are drawn from statements on his official House website; roll-call votes themselves are not listed here as they are added separately by script.

candidates.name: Jessica Killin
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary over Joe Reagan.

summary.text: Jessica Killin is the Democratic nominee for Colorado's 5th Congressional District. A Colorado Springs native and U.S. Army veteran with a Georgetown law degree, she worked at USAA and as a congressional and White House staffer, including as chief of staff to Second Gentleman Doug Emhoff. She describes her campaign as focused on affordability, anti-corruption measures and veterans' care.

background.text: Grew up on the east side of Colorado Springs, the child of a public school educator, and graduated from Falcon High School, according to her Ballotpedia survey.

Earned an ROTC scholarship and served in the U.S. Army as a Captain and paratrooper and as a Military Police Officer, per her Ballotpedia survey; the Colorado Sun reports she served from 1995 to 2003, including peacekeeping deployments in the Balkans.
Earned a law degree from Georgetown University.
Spent over a decade at USAA, according to her Ballotpedia survey; the Colorado Sun reports she worked as a lobbyist for the company.
Worked as chief of staff to Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez and to then-Reps. Carolyn Maloney and Donna Shalala, and as an aide to then-Sens. Bill Nelson and Tom Carper, according to the Colorado Sun.
Joined Second Gentleman Doug Emhoff's office as chief of staff in 2023; her White House title included deputy assistant to the President, per the Colorado Sun.
Returned to the 5th District in June 2025 and launched her campaign, according to the Colorado Sun.
Won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary over Joe Reagan, 61.2% to 38.8%.
Describes herself as a mother in a blended family with her husband, Raj, and three children.

priorities.text: Says the district faces an affordability crisis in housing, healthcare, childcare and groceries, and would work to end tariffs she says are driving up prices and to reverse Medicaid cuts.
Says she would push to ban members of Congress from trading individual stocks, strengthen ethics rules, end congressional pay during shutdowns, and create an independent Congressional Ethics Office.
Says she would prioritize fully staffing VA clinics, restoring funding for the Veterans Crisis Line, and protecting military families from housing or employment discrimination.

positions.summary: Says she will work to end tariffs she describes as driving up prices, which she says Crank has repeatedly voted to protect.
positions.quote: I will end the harmful tariffs that are driving up prices, which Jeff Crank has repeatedly voted to protect.

positions.summary: Says she would work to reverse Medicaid cuts that raise healthcare costs and push to lower prescription drug and insurance premium costs.
Says she would work to expand housing supply in the Pikes Peak region to improve access for first-time homebuyers.

summary.text: Mark Elworth Jr., who campaigns as "Marky Jr," is the Libertarian Party candidate for Colorado's 5th District. According to Ballotpedia he was born in Omaha, Nebraska, and worked as a salesman. In his candidate survey he says he is running to challenge the two-party system, cut government spending and legalize marijuana nationwide.

background.text: Born in Omaha, Nebraska, per Ballotpedia.
Graduated from the VanEd Educational Center in 2015 and has worked as a salesman, per Ballotpedia.
Nominated by the Libertarian Party of Colorado as its 2026 candidate for Congressional District 5.
In his Ballotpedia survey, describes himself as challenging "the 2 party system and the status quo," and says he does not accept donations.

summary.text: Christopher Mitchell is the American Constitution Party candidate for Colorado's 5th District and a repeat candidate for the seat. In a bio he submitted to KKTV in 2024, he described himself as an engineering contractor who grew up in Alamogordo, New Mexico.

background.text: In a 2024 bio submitted to KKTV, listed his hometown as Alamogordo, New Mexico, and said he had lived in the 5th District for 24 years.
In the same bio, listed a Bachelor of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering from New Mexico State University and a profession of engineering contractor.
Was the American Constitution Party candidate for the 5th District in 2024 and reported no previously held elected positions.

researchNotes: Steven Fuller, an unaffiliated write-in candidate, is also listed by Ballotpedia as running in the general election but has no public campaign footprint found and is omitted here. No Ballotpedia biography page exists for Christopher Mitchell (American Constitution Party); only his ballot listing was found. No stated issue positions were found for Crank beyond his committee assignments and one interview quote; his official and campaign social-media accounts were not reviewed for this basic-tier entry. Biography gaps: Mark Elworth Jr. and Christopher Mitchell have little public biography (Mitchell's comes from a 2024 self-submitted KKTV bio); later Ballotpedia coverage also lists additional unaffiliated candidates not included here.
